posts.text:
Sixty-one years after the Voting Rights Act became law, its promise is once again under attack.
They target Black voting power first because they believe we are the easiest to silence—but their ultimate goal is to dismantle democracy for us all.

As I told @MichaelSteele last night: We have the power. We have the agency. We have the numbers. And every time we rise, unite and vote, we prove that our power is real.

posts.text:
Donald Trump just used a primetime address to relitigate an election he lost six years ago — and to demand new laws making it harder to vote.

Americans see through the lies. He tried this in Georgia first: a call to "find 11,780 votes," a raid on Fulton County, and now a war on the ballot itself.

That's not democracy. That's cowardice. America, we've beaten it before.
posts.summary: Accuses Trump of relitigating lost election and pushing voter suppression laws; references Georgia phone call

posts.text:
Children can’t vote, but their hunger is real. Yet, once again, Gov. Brian Kemp has refused to help — vetoing funding for summer nutritional assistance. Georgia families are struggling to afford groceries, rent and health care, and this would be a lifeline. During this election season remember that your elected officials should serve you and the needs of your community. If you're in need of assistance, visit: feedinggeorgia.org

Link

posts.text:
For more than a decade, Georgia has left billions of dollars on the table that could have kept hospitals open and helped our neighbors get the care they need.

Nine rural hospitals have closed. Rick Jackson says the consequences aren’t “as bad as anybody else thinks.”

It is easy to dismiss the consequences when you will never have to bear them. Georgians deserve a governor who knows the difference.
